## What the data says
- No PSI microgravity test run covers thin fabric at 30 % O₂ and 70.3 kPa; the predictor reports "NO TEST DATA" for this material class [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- The nearest PSI evidence are droplet tests of methanol (8 runs) at 30-34 % O₂ and 71.2-72.1 kPa, all "sustained" with 100 % of runs burning [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant materials (silicone, Nomex) were tested only up to 22.2 % O₂; 3 of 4 Nomex runs burned and 0 of 4 silicone runs burned (total 3/8 burned) [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- Outside PSI, Nomex HT90-40 failed NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at 30 % O₂ and 70.1 kPa in 1 g (NTRS 20070018178).
- Partial-gravity combustion data are absent in PSI; NASA FM2 researchers note that flame-spread oxygen requirements may be lowest near lunar gravity, making partial gravity potentially more hazardous than both micro- and Earth-gravity (NTRS 20260000646).

## How confident we can be
- Evidence coverage for solids is weak: 131 of 134 ordinary solid runs were "sustained"; only 2 extinction-velocity limits and 1 no-ignition run exist, so a flammability limit cannot be located [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99].
- Thin fabric has zero test runs at the target atmosphere, so confidence in any prediction is limited to the physics estimate (not a measurement).
- Droplet data provide high evidence coverage (0.892) for nearby conditions, but they involve liquid fuels, not fabric.

## Gaps
- No microgravity test data for thin fabric at 30 % O₂, 70 kPa, or any pressure below 101.3 kPa.
- No partial-gravity (lunar-gravity) combustion experiments for any material class.
- No fire-resistant material runs at oxygen levels above 22.2 %.
- Pressure range in PSI solid tests is confined to ~101 kPa; target pressure (70.3 kPa) is untested.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Conduct thin-fabric ignition and flame-spread tests at 30 % O₂ and ~70 kPa in microgravity to provide direct evidence.
- Perform partial-gravity (≈0.166 g) combustion tests for thin fabrics, fire-resistant materials, and representative solids to assess the "more hazardous" regime indicated by FM2.
- Extend solid-material pressure envelope down to 70 kPa to evaluate pressure effects on flammability limits.
- Test fire-resistant materials (silicone, Nomex) at oxygen concentrations ≥30 % to determine their behavior in the proposed rover atmosphere.
